role.altitude: The accountant stops assembling close packs, VAT returns and reconciliations by hand. Instead they own the rule set, checks and prompts that produce them from AFAS, and spend their time on judgement: tax positions, estimates, control design and what the numbers mean for the business.
reach: Bookkeeper: exception handling on unmatched bank lines and invoices once matching runs automatically
FP&A Analyst: month-end variance commentary and the actuals bridge into the forecast
Controller: first draft of the monthly management pack and the audit file for the external auditor
Payroll Specialist: monthly reconciliation of payroll journals and loonheffing to the general ledger
Credit and Collections Officer: DSO analysis and the bad-debt provision calculation
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: reconciling flex worker hours from agency portals to agency invoices and cost centres
role.ceiling_note: Roughly 25 to 35 percent of the role's hours can be freed. The ceiling is set by sign-off liability (the external auditor, the Belastingdienst and the Finance Director need a named person), by AFAS data quality and posting discipline at the three sites, and by judgement work such as provisions, tax positions and conversations with colleagues. AI drafts that work but cannot own it.
skills_to_grow: Writing reconciliation and control rules as testable specifications (AFAS GetConnectors, Power Query, SQL)
Reviewing AI-drafted reports and tax workings critically and documenting that review for the auditor
Data lineage from AFAS through the nightly Power BI extract
IT general controls and access management in AFAS Profit (segregation of duties)
Dutch tax developments (Vpb, btw, transfer of flex labour costs, earnings stripping) at the level of judgement, not computation
Explaining numbers to site managers and the OR in plain language
role.ambitious_version: A continuous close: AFAS subledgers are reconciled every night, anomalies are flagged the next morning, and the btw position and Vpb estimate are always current. Day 2 brings a draft management pack with commentary per site. The two accountants spend most of their time on a rolling controls programme, cost-to-serve per customer and site, and an audit file that is always ready. Days to close could fall from about eight to three.

tasks.short: Write the monthly finance report for management: P&L per site, cash, key variances with comments.

today.trigger: Month-end close done, Finance Director wants the management pack around working day 6 to 8.
steps: Export trial balance and cost centre data from AFAS into Excel
Refresh Power BI finance dashboard and copy charts
Compare actuals with budget and last year per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo)
Chase site managers and bookkeepers for explanations of large variances
Write commentary in Word/PowerPoint and send to Controller for review
drudgery: Copy-pasting numbers and charts into slides
Re-checking that the Excel totals tie to AFAS
Rewriting the same variance phrasing every month
today.time_sinks: Collecting explanations for variances by mail and Teams, and reconciling Excel versions with late AFAS postings.

lenses.faster: The pack builds itself from the AFAS extract with numbers tied to the trial balance; an LLM drafts variance commentary from the data and from notes site managers leave in a Teams form.
lenses.autonomous: When the period is locked in AFAS, the pack is generated overnight and the accountant gets a draft with flagged variances above threshold.
lenses.ambitious: A short pack per site and per major customer every month, plus a mid-month flash on flex labour and fuel costs, which are the biggest swing items.
lenses.joy: No more slide formatting or tying totals by hand; what is left is understanding why Venlo's margin moved and saying it clearly.
lenses.options: Generate three versions of the commentary (for the board, for site managers, for the OR's economic briefing) from the same numbers.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the report definition, thresholds and commentary rules and reviews the output, instead of building the pack.
reach: Controller: first draft of the board pack

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which variance matters to the business, checking the story against what happened on the warehouse floor, and owning the message to management.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across AFAS, Power BI and site input, with exceptions; the numbers are deterministic but the commentary is an LLM draft that a person must approve before it goes to management.

in_practice.trigger: Period status set to closed in AFAS Profit.
steps: Pull trial balance and cost centre data via AFAS GetConnector, tie totals to the ledger
Compute variances against budget and last year, flag items above set thresholds
Collect site explanations through a Teams form sent automatically for flagged items
LLM drafts commentary per site using numbers and site notes only
Accountant edits and approves; Controller signs off before distribution
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant reviews every comment and number; Controller approves the pack before it goes to the Finance Director and management.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or an LLM via API
data_needed: Trial balance per period and cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint finance close folder with version history and the approval record.

evidence.claim: Power BI can generate narrative summaries of report visuals with Copilot.
LLMs can draft variance commentary from structured variance tables when constrained to the given numbers.

risks: Commentary states a cause that is not true (made-up explanation)
Numbers in the text drift from the tables
Late AFAS postings after generation make the pack stale
research_questions: How many hours per month go into the pack today, split by data gathering and writing?
Do site managers actually provide variance reasons in a structured form if asked?
How often does management change the pack layout, and would a fixed template hold?

tasks.short: Prepare the btw return and Vpb estimates and filings, check ICP and that payments to the Belastingdienst are on time.

today.trigger: Monthly or quarterly VAT deadline; annual Vpb return and provisional assessments.
steps: Run the btw report in AFAS and reconcile VAT accounts to the ledger
Check reverse-charge, intra-EU (ICP) and foreign-VAT postings for errors
Correct mis-coded invoices with bookkeepers
File the aangifte omzetbelasting and ICP return and schedule payment in Rabobank
Prepare Vpb workings for the tax adviser and annual return
drudgery: Line-by-line checks of VAT codes on hundreds of invoices
Rebuilding the same Excel reconciliation each period
today.time_sinks: Finding and fixing wrong VAT codes on purchase and sales invoices, especially cross-border transport and agency invoices.

lenses.faster: Rule-based checks flag wrong VAT codes against supplier country, VAT number and service type before the return is drafted, so the reconciliation is mostly done when the period closes.
lenses.autonomous: Every night each new invoice is checked against VAT rules and the VIES validity check; exceptions go to the bookkeeper queue the next day.
lenses.ambitious: A current btw and Vpb position every week instead of at filing time, with a defended file for each judgement call for the tax adviser and a Belastingdienst audit.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scanning VAT codes; what remains is the interesting cross-border and fiscal questions.
lenses.options: Model Vpb scenarios (investment deduction, depreciation choices, timing of provisions) side by side for the Finance Director.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the VAT rule set and the tax control framework and reviews exceptions rather than lines.
reach: Bookkeeper: VAT code corrections at entry
Payroll Specialist: reconciling loonheffing returns to ledger

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting VAT treatment of unusual cross-border services, deciding tax positions with the adviser, and signing off a return that carries legal liability.
tasks.pattern_why: VAT rules and reconciliation are written-down logic on structured AFAS data with checkable output; no model is needed for the core, only for explaining odd cases.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly run on new AFAS invoices; period-end trigger for the return draft.
steps: Validate VAT code against supplier/customer country, VAT number (VIES) and item type
Queue exceptions for bookkeepers with suggested correct code
At period end reconcile VAT accounts to the draft return and ICP listing
Accountant reviews differences and files through AFAS/Digipoort
Payment batch prepared in Rabobank for approval
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves the return before filing; Finance Director authorises the payment batch.
data_needed: Invoice lines with VAT codes, country and VAT numbers
in_practice.logs_to: Tax file on SharePoint with reconciliation, exceptions list and filed return.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports preparing and submitting the Dutch VAT return electronically.
EU VAT number validation can be automated through the VIES service.

risks: Rule table out of date after law changes
Over-trust in automated checks leads to missed unusual transactions
Fines for late or wrong filings stay with the company
research_questions: How many VAT corrections per period are found today, and where do they come from?
Does the external tax adviser accept an automated reconciliation as working papers?
Which share of invoices is cross-border or reverse-charge?

tasks.short: Review balance sheet and P&L accounts each month: fixed assets, provisions, accruals, equity, unusual income or costs.

steps: Export balances from AFAS and compare with last month and budget
Open account details for movements that look odd
Check fixed asset register, accruals and provisions against support
Ask bookkeepers and site staff about unclear postings
Post corrections and file the review
drudgery: Ticking lines in Excel against bank or invoice support
today.time_sinks: Finding the few strange postings among thousands of normal ones, and waiting for answers.

lenses.faster: Anomaly scoring on all journal lines and automated balance-sheet reconciliations take the review straight to the twenty lines worth a look.
lenses.autonomous: Daily reconciliation of bank, AP, AR and payroll subledgers to the GL with alerts when differences arise.
lenses.ambitious: Every balance sheet account reconciled every month with support attached, not just the material ones, so audit adjustments drop toward zero.
lenses.joy: Removes the ticking and scrolling; keeps the detective work on real anomalies.
lenses.options: Show alternative explanations for each flagged movement (timing, misclassification, duplicate, real event) with the evidence for each.
lenses.altitude: Accountant sets materiality thresholds and rules and reviews flagged items and rule performance.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a provision or accrual is reasonable and knowing the operational story behind a posting.
tasks.pattern_why: Reconciliations are deterministic, but investigating anomalies needs several tools, reading documents and asking people; a person approves corrections.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and period-end close.
steps: Reconcile subledgers to GL and bank statements automatically
Score journal lines for anomalies (unusual amount, account, user, timing)
Agent gathers support (invoice, contract, email) for flagged lines and proposes an explanation
Accountant reviews, accepts or posts correction
in_practice.human_gate: Every proposed correction is approved by the accountant before posting in AFAS.
data_needed: GL detail with user and timestamp
in_practice.logs_to: Reconciliation workpapers on SharePoint with reviewer and date.

evidence.claim: Machine learning tools score all general ledger transactions for risk and anomalies.
Account reconciliation software automates balance sheet reconciliations.

risks: Too many false positives and the flags get ignored
Missing data in AFAS (no attachments) limits the evidence the agent can find
Over-reliance hides judgement areas such as provisions
research_questions: How many audit adjustments last year came from balance sheet accounts that were not reconciled?
What share of AFAS postings have an attached document?
Is a BlackLine-type tool affordable at this size, or is Power Query plus rules enough?

tasks.short: Write up findings from internal checks and the external audit: what went wrong, impact, fix, owner.

today.trigger: End of an internal control test, interim audit, or the auditor's management letter.
steps: Collect test results and notes from Excel and email
Describe each finding, its cause and financial impact
Agree actions and owners with the Controller and process owners
Write the report in Word and track follow-up in Excel
drudgery: Turning messy notes into consistent finding write-ups
today.time_sinks: Rewriting findings into a standard format and chasing owners for action dates.

lenses.faster: An LLM turns test sheets and notes into findings in a fixed format (condition, criterion, cause, effect, action) for the accountant to edit.
lenses.autonomous: Follow-up reminders and status updates for open findings run from a SharePoint list without manual chasing.
lenses.ambitious: Every control test produces a finding record, so management sees a live view of control health instead of a yearly letter.
lenses.joy: Less rewriting; more time to discuss fixes with process owners.
lenses.options: Draft several remediation options per finding with effort and risk for the Controller to choose.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs the finding template and rating scale and reviews drafts.
reach: Controller: drafting the response to the auditor's management letter

tasks.human_edge: Rating severity, agreeing fixes with colleagues, and the tact needed when a finding points at someone's work.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is unstructured notes and the output carries judgement and sensitivity; the person leads, AI drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Control test or audit item marked complete in the SharePoint tracker.
steps: Upload test workpapers and notes
LLM drafts findings in the standard template
Accountant edits severity and wording, agrees actions with owners
Report published and follow-ups scheduled automatically
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Controller approve every finding before it is shared.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint findings list with status history.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word drafts documents from referenced files.

risks: Draft overstates or understates severity
Sensitive personal remarks end up in the report (AVG)
research_questions: How many findings per year are written, and how long does each take?
Would the external auditor accept the standard template for follow-up?
Does the Controller want severity ratings standardised?

tasks.short: Work out the company's tax position: deferred taxes, fiscal depreciation, valuation differences, interest deduction limits.

today.trigger: Year-end, provisional Vpb assessment, or a big investment such as new trucks or racking.
steps: Build the commercial-to-fiscal reconciliation in Excel
Calculate fiscal depreciation and deferred tax per asset group
Check the earnings stripping limit and other deductions
Discuss positions with the external tax adviser
Book the tax charge and deferred tax in AFAS
drudgery: Maintaining a separate fiscal asset register in Excel
Rolling forward the same spreadsheets each year
today.time_sinks: Keeping commercial and fiscal registers in step and reworking the file after the adviser's comments.

lenses.faster: A fiscal register next to the AFAS asset register computes fiscal depreciation and deferred tax automatically each month.
lenses.autonomous: The deferred tax and current tax estimate update monthly after close without a manual run.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly tax charge in the management pack instead of a year-end surprise, and investment decisions modelled for tax effect before they are made.
lenses.joy: No more rolling Excel forward; the time goes to tax planning conversations.
lenses.options: Scenarios for timing of investments, depreciation methods and use of investment deduction schemes.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the fiscal rules and checks the model; the adviser reviews positions.
reach: FP&A Analyst: tax line in the forecast

tasks.human_edge: Choosing and defending tax positions with the adviser and the Belastingdienst; liability stays with people.
tasks.pattern_why: Fiscal depreciation and deferred tax follow written rules on structured asset data; a calculation tool beats a model here.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly close and new asset additions in AFAS.
steps: Sync asset additions and disposals from AFAS
Apply fiscal depreciation rules and compute differences
Compute current and deferred tax estimate
Accountant reviews and posts the tax journal
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves the tax journal; tax positions agreed with the external adviser and Finance Director.
systems: Excel or a small tax calculation app
in_practice.logs_to: Tax file on SharePoint with monthly calculation snapshots.

evidence.claim: Deferred tax and fiscal depreciation calculations can be automated from an asset register with fixed rules.

risks: Wrong rule entered once repeats every month
Tax law changes not reflected
Over-precision gives false confidence in an estimate
research_questions: How large are commercial-fiscal differences in practice, and is the effort worth it?
Does the tax adviser already have a tool that could take this over?
How often do positions change after adviser review?

tasks.short: Check AFAS and linked systems for control gaps: access rights, interfaces, approvals; propose fixes.

today.trigger: Yearly IT controls review, auditor request, or a system change such as a new staffing agency feed.
steps: Export user roles and authorisations from AFAS
Check segregation of duties (who can create suppliers and pay them)
Test interfaces: agency hours and invoices, Rabobank, Power BI extract
Write recommendations and discuss them with IT and the Controller
drudgery: Matching user lists against role matrices by hand
today.time_sinks: Interpreting AFAS authorisation exports and tracing interface errors back to their source.

lenses.faster: A script checks AFAS roles against a segregation-of-duties matrix and lists conflicts in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly automatic checks on user rights, master data changes (supplier bank accounts) and interface record counts, with alerts.
lenses.ambitious: Continuous control monitoring of the three agency feeds and payments, catching fraud and duplicate invoices before payment.
lenses.joy: Less export-and-compare; more design of better controls.
lenses.options: Several control designs per risk, with cost and friction for the sites.
lenses.altitude: Accountant designs the control set and monitors its health.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: AFAS role hygiene

tasks.human_edge: Judging which risks matter, balancing control against workload, and persuading IT and site managers to change.
tasks.pattern_why: The checks can be scripted, but evaluation and recommendations need judgement; AI helps analyse and draft.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule and any AFAS role or interface change.
steps: Export roles, master data change logs and interface counts
Run SoD and change checks
LLM summarises conflicts and drafts recommendations
Accountant reviews with Controller and IT
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Controller decide on control changes; IT implements.

evidence.claim: Segregation-of-duties conflict checks can be scripted from role exports.

risks: Incomplete exports give false comfort
Access data includes personal data (AVG)
research_questions: Can AFAS export role and authorisation data in a usable form?
Has the auditor flagged IT general controls before?
How are supplier bank account changes approved today?

tasks.short: Prepare and check the annual accounts and monthly statements under Dutch GAAP (Titel 9 BW 2) for the auditor.

today.trigger: Year-end and monthly statements; external audit planning.
steps: Map the AFAS trial balance to the annual accounts layout
Prepare notes and disclosures in Word/Excel
Build the audit file with reconciliations and support
Answer auditor questions and process adjustments
drudgery: Cross-checking totals between statements and notes
today.time_sinks: Re-doing the notes after late adjustments and answering long auditor request lists.

lenses.faster: Linked statements and notes update from the trial balance mapping, with automated tie-out checks.
lenses.autonomous: The audit file builds itself from monthly reconciliations so year-end is mostly a review.
lenses.ambitious: Quarterly mini-closes in annual-accounts quality, so year-end becomes the fourth quarter close.
lenses.joy: No more cross-footing by hand; keeps the judgement in estimates and disclosures.
lenses.options: Draft disclosure wording for new items in several versions for the Controller.
lenses.altitude: Accountant maintains the mapping and checks and reviews the draft.

tasks.human_edge: Accounting judgements, disclosures and the relationship with the auditor.
tasks.pattern_why: Mapping and tie-outs are deterministic; note drafting and auditor requests need an LLM; all output is reviewed.

in_practice.trigger: Year-end close and auditor request list.
steps: Map trial balance to statement layout
Generate statements and notes with tie-out checks
LLM drafts note text and answers to auditor requests from the file
Accountant reviews and Controller signs off
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Finance Director approve the accounts; auditor signs the opinion.

evidence.claim: Excel linked to the ledger with Copilot can help draft and check financial statements.

risks: Mapping error spreads through all statements
Disclosure text does not match Dutch GAAP requirements
research_questions: How many hours does year-end take today, and what share is tie-out?
Will the auditor accept an automatically built audit file?
Is the AFAS chart of accounts stable enough for fixed mapping?

tasks.short: Check records and talk to colleagues at the sites to confirm transactions are booked right and rules are followed.

today.trigger: Internal control tests, odd postings, or auditor questions.
steps: Select samples of transactions
Ask site staff and bookkeepers how they process them
Compare with procedures and laws
Record results and follow up
today.time_sinks: Arranging and holding conversations across three sites.

lenses.faster: Samples and supporting documents are pulled automatically; interview notes are transcribed and summarised.
lenses.autonomous: Risk-based sampling runs monthly and queues the transactions to review.
lenses.ambitious: Regular walk-throughs at all three sites instead of only when the auditor asks.
lenses.joy: Less admin; more time with colleagues on the floor.
lenses.options: Interview question sets tailored per process and site.
lenses.altitude: Accountant designs the sampling and review approach.

tasks.human_edge: Trust and judgement in conversations with colleagues; noticing what is not said.
tasks.pattern_why: The core is talking to people and judging compliance; AI only supports preparation and notes.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly sample schedule or flagged anomaly.
steps: Risk-based sample pulled from AFAS with documents
Accountant interviews staff (notes transcribed with consent)
LLM summarises and drafts finding
Accountant concludes

evidence.claim: Teams meetings can be transcribed and summarised by Copilot.

risks: Recording conversations raises AVG and OR concerns
Staff speak less openly when recorded
research_questions: Would the OR agree to transcription of control interviews?
How many interviews per year happen today?
Which processes have the most compliance issues?
